reviewer: Claude Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5) as the local agent, the same session that drives the cycle

findings.task_step: Submit with an invalid email after filling the other fields
findings.observed: Before the rejected submit the form held name 'Alex Morgan', email 'alex@' and a request; after it all three fields are empty and only 'Please check your details and try again.' remains.
findings.principle: Preserve completed work; error recovery must not cost the user their valid entries (task acceptance: 'A rejected email preserves the entered name and request')
findings.likely_consequence: Inference: the user must retype the whole request to correct one character, and some will abandon the form.
findings.confidence_reason: The before and after field values are captured directly in the observations.
findings.proposed_correction: Do not reset the form on a validation failure; validate each field and keep every entered value.
findings.verification: Rerun test_invalid_email_preserves_work_and_can_complete: name and request survive the rejected submit and the corrected email completes.

findings.observed: The only feedback is the generic line 'Please check your details and try again.'; no field is marked and nothing says what is missing or how to fix it.
findings.principle: Help people recognise, diagnose and recover from errors: say which field and what would make it acceptable (task acceptance: 'Missing or invalid information is identified with a useful correction')
findings.likely_consequence: Inference: users guess which field failed; screen-reader users get no field-level cue.
findings.confidence_reason: The visible text and screenshot show no per-field message.
findings.proposed_correction: Write a specific message into each field's existing *-error slot, set aria-invalid on the field, and keep a summary in #feedback.

findings.task_step: Recover from a failed submit using the keyboard
findings.observed: After every failed submit the focused element is the Send request button, not the field that needs correcting.
findings.principle: Keyboard operability and error identification: after a failed submit, focus goes to the first problem (task acceptance: 'Keyboard users can discover the error and correct it')
findings.likely_consequence: Inference: keyboard and screen-reader users must hunt backwards through the form to find the problem.
findings.confidence_reason: focused_element is captured in each failing observation.
findings.proposed_correction: Move focus to the first invalid field after a failed submit.

remaining_uncertainty: The sending, cancel and temporary-failure paths passed and were reviewed only through their captures. Whether #feedback stays inside a 375px viewport after an error cannot be judged from a full-page screenshot; cycle 001 recorded that as an unresolved question and this review does not repeat it. Colour contrast of the error style was not measured.
